answer: According to the Wikipedia document corpus, chlorophyll a is the main photosynthetic pigment in plants. It is described as "a specific form of chlorophyll used in oxygenic photosynthesis" and is "essential for photosynthesis in eukaryotes, cyanobacteria and prochlorophytes because of its role as primary electron donor in the electron transport chain." Chlorophyll a absorbs most strongly from the violet-blue and orange-red ranges of light, while it is a poor absorber of green and near-green portions of the spectrum (which is why chlorophyll-containing tissues appear green, as green light is diffusively reflected by structures like cell walls).
